speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to Dr. Agent's office. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; to help me narrow down the cause, could you describe exactly where the pain is located and what specific movements trigger it? Also, did this start suddenly after an injury or does it come on gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain radiating to your elbow and worsening when holding your baby suggests potential involvement of the median nerve or a complex regional pain syndrome; did you notice any numbness or tingling in your thumb and index finger? REQUEST TEST: Nerve_Conduction_Study

speaker: Doctor
text: The nerve conduction study results appear normal, which makes a primary nerve compression less likely. Given your history of falling on an outstretched hand and pain that radiates to the elbow, could you describe if you have noticed any swelling, bruising, or a deformity in your wrist at the site of the fall? REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_Wrist
